profile.org_note: One reportable segment, run centrally from Las Vegas, NV (headquarters) and Calabasas, CA (investor relations and certain corporate functions), with 28 more leased offices in 16 states for operations and development staff. Only three people are executive officers: CEO Bryan Smith, CFO Chris Lau (whose published remit includes treasury and capital markets) and CAO/CLO Sara Vogt-Lowell; the 10-Q names the CEO and COO as the chief operating decision maker. AMH Development, the in-house homebuilding arm, was led by an Executive Vice President of Development (Brent Landry, per a 2024 company release); market-level development and land leaders are not published, and the only named regional leader is on the property-operations side (Florida). States listed are those with AMH-built communities on communities.amh.com; markets listed are the 14 metros with 2026 development deliveries and lots. The rental portfolio as a whole spans 24 states and 30+ markets.
profile.summary: Single-family-rental REIT (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa2) that builds homes to keep and rent, not to sell: 60,626 operating homes in 24 states plus 4,068 in joint ventures at 2026-09-30. AMH Development delivered 2,322 homes in 2025 (1,879 wholly owned, 443 to two 20%-owned joint ventures) and guides to 1,700 to 2,100 in 2026; its land pipeline has been cut from about 14,000 lots in 2022 to 5,422 at 2026-09-30 (5,066 owned, 356 optioned), with the most lots in Atlanta, Phoenix, Seattle and Charleston. Plausible but low-priority land-banking customer: the 10-K says it has used land-banking arrangements and may again, but it unwound its one disclosed arrangement in 2025 (land sold to an unnamed land banker in 2022 with finished-lot buyback options; consolidated land not owned fell from $89.7 million at year-end 2024 to zero at year-end 2025), owns about 93% of its lots, borrows unsecured at a 4.48% average rate, and is slowing development to fund share buybacks, so near-term need is small.
